findings.note: None of the six test logs in this bundle describes the code in this bundle. Every log ends `RESULT: 102 passed, 0 failed` and its PASS lines enumerate exactly six T-003 invocations (affected-component-resolution-failed, contract-discovery-failed, registry-validation-failed, dependency-subprocess-failed, dsl-warn-unmatched-trigger, dsl-warn-matched-nondetermining) and no T-004 section. The shipped driver's main() runs ten cases through run_t003_case() and four more through run_t004_case(); counting its own counts.check() calls gives 141 assertions (36 CASES + 22 projection + 12 projection-block + 50 T-003 + 19 T-004 + 2 registration), and 102 is exactly the same arithmetic with the six-case T-003 list and no T-004 list. The implementation itself has likewise moved on (module docstring now reads 'T-002+T-003+T-004 (steps 0-13)', and the AC-056 multi-entry diagnostics[] behaviour in _write_evidence/_evaluate_capabilities changes the Resolver Evidence document the dsl-warn-* fixtures assert). The RED/GREEN pair and both focused-test runs are therefore evidence for bytes that no longer exist; nothing in this bundle shows the reviewed implementation passing anything.

The contract's stated reason for accepting the un-recaptured RED/GREEN pair is falsified by the bundle's own contents. It argues: 'the live staged ... resolve-project-context.py is byte-identical (sha256 7d59debc63422f9ea20ab4042343d3284dade87f6bb0aad69ee77c7214da19ed) to the report's own Outputs-table claim, so the recorded green-sh.log/green-ps1.log ... describe the exact code this contract also just re-ran.' The bundle flags that path's declared hash STALE, and the current human-copy/MANIFEST.sha256 carried in this same bundle records ca3c95f6516064dc3540fd4959f5ff1e78adf67a8c61ffd995304864c1cb836b for it. The identity premise is false, so `unit-tests: passes: true` and `acceptance-tests: passes: true` rest on evidence for other code. The same comment also still narrates task-state-check as 'recorded below as passes:false/required:true' while the check block records passes:true, reconciled only by an appended re-record sentence.

AC-024 locks `diagnostics[]` sorted by `(id, detail)`. _write_evidence builds `list(warn_diagnostics or []) + [{block entry}]`. On the dsl-warn path every entry carries the identical id `dsl-warn-on-matched-capability`, and the block entry's detail ('a predicate evaluation produced an outcome: warn evidence node') is a strict prefix of every warn entry's detail ('... warn evidence node at capability_id=...'), so an (id, detail) sort places the block entry FIRST. The emitted order puts it last. The driver's expectation (`expected_warn_diagnostics + [{block}]` in run_t003_case) reproduces the emitted order rather than the specified one, so the 'exact Resolver Evidence' assertion cannot catch the violation.

A launch failure of validate-capability-registry (OSError: missing, unreadable, or non-executable dependency) is raised as RegistryValidationFailed and reported to the caller as 'capability-registry.json failed validate-capability-registry checks' -- blaming the project's Registry for a local environment fault, and emitting a diagnostic id whose REQ-002 meaning is a Registry defect. This contradicts the rule the same file states at step 4, where the OSError case is deliberately folded into DependencySubprocessFailed on the explicit claim that this is 'the SAME closed-enum, fixed-sentence DependencySubprocessFailed path steps 5/6/7-8 already use for an identical OSError'. Steps 6 and 7-8 do; step 5 does not. No fixture in the bundle exercises a validate-capability-registry launch failure, so the mismatch is unguarded.

design.md step 6 requires `generate-registry-digest --whole` be run 'against the located Registry', and step 5's B8 snapshot rule requires 'the located Registry's own canonicalized bytes' be retained in memory as this invocation's fixed Registry snapshot. Neither is implemented: _discover_registry keeps only a json.load()ed dict and discards the path's canonical form, and _generate_registry_digest_whole passes no path at all, relying on the dependency repeating ADR-0025 discovery on its own. The identity of the two discoveries is asserted only in a docstring; nothing in the bundle demonstrates it, and no fixture makes the two resolutions diverge. registry_digest is the provenance field written into context_binding on a task recorded Security-Sensitive: true, so an unbound digest is an integrity gap, not a stylistic one.

The expected Evidence is recomputed with properties the resolver does not use. The driver calls real_evaluate_predicate(predicate, {"characteristics": {"pii": True}}) for comp-a and real_evaluate_predicate(predicate, {}) for comp-b, while _evaluate_capabilities passes projection_components.get(component_id, {}) -- the full Context-Projection entry, which for both fixtures also carries `paths`. design.md step 7 fixes `--component-properties <this affected component's Context-Projection entry>`; because the expectation is built from a hand-narrowed subset, the assertion cannot fail if the resolver hands evaluate-predicate a truncated, substituted, or wrongly-keyed properties document, provided `characteristics` survives. That is precisely the contract these two fixtures are cited as covering.

Four of the ten T-003 cases the shipped driver executes have no fixture content anywhere in the bundle, and no log exercises them. run_t003_case unconditionally copies `fixture_dir/project-context.yaml` and, for three of them, a stub or registry from the same directory, so those directories must exist -- but they are not declared outputs and their bytes are unavailable. Their assertions are unverifiable claims, including the only test of the ascending-lexicographic affected-component fan-out (dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components), which is REQ-005/AC-024 determinism named explicitly in T-003's own Requirements line. Every other fixture in the bundle supplies a single affected component or an already-sorted pair, so the `sorted(affected_components)` at the fan-out is otherwise never load-bearing.

The CHANGELOG entry -- a declared T-003 output covering AC-033 -- states '5 diagnostic rows / 6 invocations' and 'sh/ps1 both 102 passed / 0 failed'. The shipped suite runs fourteen post-projection invocations and 141 assertions. The declared output is now inaccurate about the very change it documents.

The evidence backing `requirement-traceability: passes: true` cites 'CASE_NAMES list (line 160-165)' enumerating 'exactly T-003's own six fixtures' and 'the four assertions they each carry'. The shipped driver has no CASE_NAMES symbol (it is ALL_CASE_NAMES, fourteen post-projection names) and each T-003 case carries five assertions. The check was computed against a different file, so its PASS does not transfer to the reviewed driver.

`sys.path.insert(0, str(script_dir))` is never undone, so for the remainder of the process any later import resolves against the script directory ahead of the standard library. On a Security-Sensitive path this is an avoidable widening; a try/finally restore, or importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, would keep the import local.

design.md's step-4 invocation is `resolve-component-paths --config <same> [--source-rev <same>] --target-rev <same> [--include-untracked] --json`, with the bracketed flags passed only when supplied. The implementation always passes --source-rev (defaulting to 'HEAD') and always passes one of --include-untracked / --no-include-untracked; `--no-include-untracked` appears in neither design.md nor any Epic A3 contract text carried in this bundle, and the dependency's acceptance of that flag cannot be verified from the material provided.
